issues.legal_issue: A writ petition challenging a consolidation scheme may be dismissed in limine when the challenge is brought after years of inaction and omits landholders likely to be affected by disturbing the scheme.
material_facts: The appellants challenged a village consolidation scheme only after years without raising objections to it.
Other landholders were likely to be affected if the scheme were disturbed, but they were not joined in the writ petition.
The High Court dismissed the writ petition in limine.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was justified in dismissing the writ petition in limine, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A delayed challenge to a consolidation scheme may be dismissed where the petitioners failed to object for years and did not join landholders likely to be affected by disturbing the scheme.

predicates.writ_challenges_consolidation_scheme: The petitioners brought a writ petition challenging a consolidation scheme.
predicates.challenge_delayed_for_years: The petitioners let years pass without raising an objection to the scheme.
predicates.affected_landholders_not_joined: The petitioners did not join landholders likely to be affected if the scheme were disturbed.
predicates.writ_dismissal_justified: The writ petition may be dismissed in limine.

issues.definition: When a writ petition challenges a consolidation scheme, the challenge is delayed for years, and affected landholders are not joined, dismissal of the writ petition in limine is justified.
